questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Jacob Berab was born in the Kingdom of Castile.
questions.explanation: He was born in 1474 in Maqueda, near Toledo, in the heart of Castile.

questions.question: With whom did Maharyb Berab study in his youth?
options: Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, in his yeshiva in Guadalajara
questions.explanation: Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, the "last of the Geonim" of Castile; Berab saw himself as the torchbearer of the Spanish Torah world that had been destroyed.

questions.question: How old was Berab when he went into exile in the expulsion from Spain?
questions.explanation: In the summer of 1492 the young Berab went into exile, and yet he was immediately appointed rabbi of a community.

questions.question: To which city did he come first after the expulsion, where he was appointed rabbi of the community?
questions.explanation: An appointment at such a young age attests to his early genius. From there he continued to Algiers and to Egypt.

questions.question: What did Berab do for a living in Egypt?
questions.explanation: His economic independence from commerce was one of the sources of his authority in Safed.

questions.question: What was the "Beit HaVa'ad" that Berab founded in Safed?
options: A supreme body of the sages of all the congregations, a beit din and a council for halakha and leadership
A synagogue for the Anusim only
A printing house for Kabbalistic books
A yeshiva for the children of the exiles
questions.explanation: He sought to unite the many sages who flowed into Safed from all over the Diaspora, and he also headed the "Great Yeshiva."

questions.question: True or false: Maharyb Berab initiated the renewal of semikhah in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: He renewed semikhah in Safed, claiming that most of the sages of the Land of Israel were concentrated there. The sages of Jerusalem objected.

questions.question: In which year did Berab try to renew semikhah?
questions.explanation: In the Hebrew year 5298. This was one of the most significant attempts in the history of Israel to change the legal structure of the nation.

questions.question: Whose position did Berab base himself on in renewing semikhah?
options: The Ramban: semikhah will be renewed only by a prophet
The Rambam: the agreement of all the sages of the Land of Israel renews semikhah
The Rif: any rabbi may ordain
questions.explanation: According to the Rambam, a judge whom all the sages of the Land of Israel ordained unanimously is considered ordained and may ordain others.

questions.question: What urgent need did Berab seek to resolve by renewing semikhah?
options: Appointing a chief rabbi for the Ottoman Empire
Atonement for the Anusim: those liable to karet who were lashed are released from their karet
questions.explanation: Such lashes can be administered only by a beit din of ordained judges, and Berab wanted to give the Anusim who had returned full atonement and peace of mind.

questions.question: True or false: The sages of Jerusalem, headed by the Ralbach, supported the semikhah initiative.
questions.explanation: The Ralbach objected sharply: the sages of Jerusalem were not asked and did not agree, and the Rambam required the agreement of all.

questions.question: Where was Berab forced to go as a result of the controversy?
questions.explanation: He feared denunciations to the Ottoman authorities, but before leaving he ordained four of his students, among them Rabbi Yosef Karo and the Mabit.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Yosef Karo regarded Maharyb Berab as his preeminent teacher.
questions.explanation: In the book "Maggid Meisharim" Karo is told that he merited to be ordained by virtue of his self-sacrifice for the renewal of the crown of semikhah.

questions.question: How did Rabbi Yosef Karo realize his teacher's vision of unity in a different way?
options: By establishing the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
By writing the "Shulchan Arukh," a code for all the communities of Israel
By founding a yeshiva in Constantinople
By printing his teacher's novellae on the entire Talmud
questions.explanation: The Sanhedrin was not established, but the Shulchan Arukh served as a kind of "substitute for authority" and united the people halakhically.

questions.question: True or false: All of Berab's commentaries on the Talmud were printed and have reached us.
questions.explanation: Of all his work on the Talmud, only the commentary on tractate Kiddushin has reached us.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Moshe Alshich, who was ordained by Rabbi Yosef Karo, ordained Rabbi Chaim Vital.
questions.explanation: In this way Berab's chain of semikhah became linked to the Kabbalah of Safed and to the preeminent student of the Ari.

questions.question: What argument did the Ralbach raise against the renewal of semikhah?
options: Semikhah is forbidden under foreign rule
Berab is not worthy of being ordained
The Rambam himself wrote that "the matter requires a decision"
The Anusim do not need atonement
questions.explanation: This implies that the Rambam himself was not certain. He also argued that the Ramban and others hold that semikhah will be renewed only by a prophet or with the coming of the Messiah.

questions.question: What distinguished Berab's glosses on the "Mishneh Torah"?
options: They translated the book into Spanish
They disagreed with the Rambam in every chapter
They abridged the book for the use of judges
They were written on the parts that the "Maggid Mishneh" did not explain, in order to complete it
questions.explanation: This was the first attempt to give the Rambam's code a comprehensive explanation, and in it his admiration for the Rambam, the foundation of the semikhah initiative, is evident.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Israel of Shklov try to do in the 1830s?
options: To renew semikhah by means of a letter to the Ten Lost Tribes, in the hope that it had been preserved there
To gather all the sages of Safed for a single ordination
To annul the semikhah that Berab had renewed
questions.explanation: He, one of the disciples of the Gra, sought to bypass the obstacles raised in the controversy between Berab and the Ralbach.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Yehuda Leib Maimon, the first Minister of Religions, claim in the wake of Berab's approach?
options: That Berab's approach was finally rejected
That in the State of Israel the obligation to renew the central authority is stronger than ever
That semikhah can be renewed only with the coming of the Messiah
That the Shulchan Arukh makes the Sanhedrin superfluous
questions.explanation: He saw in the State the fulfillment of the conditions that Berab sought: the return of the people to its land and the concentration of its sages in one place.
